value: field call rate of wild calling males increased with local light level (p = 0.01, chi2 = 5.9942); association across 6 urban and 7 forest sites, not a manipulation
method: observational light association: field call rate (calls in 1 min before capture) of calling male frogs compared with average light level (lux meter HT309, 0.01-400 lux, breast height, upward and four cardinal directions) at their calling sites, generalized Poisson mixed models, site as random intercept, number of simultaneously calling frogs as covariate
conditions: wild calling male tungara frogs caught at six urban and seven forest sites around Panama City, Panama, 2019 and/or 2021, 20:00 to 00:00, four calling frogs per habitat per collection night, 80 males collected in all (the number of frogs in the field model is not stated); light, noise and habitat type were collinear so light and noise were entered in separate models from site type; the same sentence reports call rate tended to increase with noise (p = 0.05); light was a site average of readings taken at calling sites, not measured at each frog; urban frogs called about twice as often as forest frogs; the paper also found no significant light by noise interaction on field call rate or maximum call complexity (all p > 0.60) and no significant association of maximum call complexity with light or noise (all p > 0.10); the laboratory exposure experiments on the wild-caught frogs are not filed

method: observational light association: spotlight-survey counts of wild Australian house geckos per night correlated with percent moon illumination (zero when the moon was below the horizon); linear mixed-effects model with site and air temperature random terms
conditions: wild geckos in open savanna woodland, Wambiana Grazing Trial, Wambiana Station, 80 km southwest of Charters Towers, Queensland; 24 one-hectare sites, two observers, nightly for one week each in July and September 2014, August 2015 and May 2016, 800 person-hours giving 644 gecko observations; moon illumination (% illuminated) taken from timeanddate.com and not measured on site, cloud cover at most 5%; counts are detections by spotlight, so detectability and activity are not separated; mixed model for moon illumination F = 29.206, df 1,45, p < 0.001, 95% CI 0.018 to 0.039; predator abundance (24 nocturnal predators) was not linked to moon illumination (snake r = -0.38, p = 0.517; bird r = 0.08, p = 0.826); artificial light was not measured in the field surveys; the laboratory emergence experiments are not filed
